models.summary: A Petri net of the wheat fields around Uppsala is filled with Lotka-Volterra energy equations. Places are wheat, ladybug, aphid, swallow, field mouse and fungus; transitions are photosynthesis, intake, predation and decomposition. Producer energy grows on solar input with a capacity and is cut by pests. The two primary consumers compete through coefficients beta one and beta two. Secondary consumers eat both insects and do not compete with each other. The decomposer draws on the deaths of every level. Seasonal corrections add a migration loss for swallows, a breeding gain for voles, and a winter capacity. After harvest the wheat term vanishes and the insects only lose energy. Chemicals remove the pest penalty and raise the capacity. A maturity index sums species richness, biomass, the production-to-respiration ratio, energy use and food-web complexity. Returning the red fox and the lynx lifts the index from 9.35 to 11.33.

models.summary: Removing the herbicide lets weeds grow and compete with wheat. Both photosynthesize, but weed energy cannot be eaten. Wheat is suppressed in proportion to weed energy and weeds in proportion to wheat energy. Searching over the ratio of the two competition coefficients puts the collapse at 2.3: above it, wheat energy tends to zero and the consumers starve. Adding bats restores the system through predation on pests and a higher photosynthetic efficiency from pollination. Woodpeckers do the same job but move the maturity index less. The printed bat result leaves the index endpoints blank.
models.purpose: Find how far the herbicide can be cut before the wheat collapses, and whether a returning species prevents it.

models.summary: A two-level fuzzy evaluation compares conventional agriculture before 2010 with organic agriculture after 2020. Four primary factors and ten secondary indicators are judged on a three-word rubric: quite positive, slightly positive, negative. Each indicator gets a Cauchy affiliation function with its own parameters, giving ten groups. Weights come from the entropy method in four steps: proportion, entropy, coefficient of variation, normalized weight. The affiliation sums on the two positive grades are 0.5462, 0.7445 and 0.2458. Pest control scores below one and cost per unit area is harmful; every other indicator favors organic agriculture.
models.purpose: Turn the organic-versus-conventional comparison into one weighted score.
objectives: Score organic agriculture against conventional agriculture on ten indicators.
